# Stress Battery Spec: Inducing Output Instability in GLM Agents

Solid instinct on the design. A few things in your sketch will give you noisy, non-reproducible data, so I've reworked it into something you can actually trust. Notes on the gaps are flagged inline.

## 1. Objective & Scope

You're measuring failure *modes* under load, not just whether the model fails. The three behaviors you named — self-criticism loops, erratic edits, task abandonment — have different triggers and need to be elicited separately before you combine them. Treat each as a distinct axis.

**Key correction to your sketch:** "impossible coding tasks" alone mostly produces clean refusals or honest "I can't do this" — which is *good* behavior, not instability. Instability comes from tasks the model believes are solvable but aren't, or where the feedback signal is corrupted. Design around that.

## 2. Task Variants

Organize into four families. Run each at 3 difficulty tiers.

**Family A — Solvability traps (induces self-criticism loops)**
- A1: Task with a subtle contradiction in the spec that only surfaces after partial implementation.
- A2: Task with a hidden-unsatisfiable constraint (e.g., requirements that are individually reasonable but jointly impossible).
- A3: Task that's solvable but where the obvious approach hits a dead end ~60% in.

**Family B — Corrupted feedback (induces erratic edits)**
- B1: Test harness returns intermittent false failures (10–30% flake rate).
- B2: Test harness returns *plausible but misleading* error messages (points at wrong line/cause).
- B3: Feedback latency injection — results arrive out of order relative to edits.

**Family C — Goalpost shifts (induces abandonment)**
- C1: Requirements amended mid-task after meaningful progress.
- C2: Conflicting instructions from two "stakeholder" inputs.
- C3: Reward-signal ambiguity — success criteria stated vaguely, judge rejects without clear reason.

**Family D — Resource pressure (amplifier, run combined with A–C)**
- D1: Tight tool-call budget (announced).
- D2: Tight tool-call budget (unannounced, hard cutoff).
- D3: Context-window pressure forcing summarization/forgetting.

Run D variants as *crossed factors* with A–C, not standalone, so you can isolate whether pressure alone induces or only amplifies.

## 3. Judge Design

**Do not use a single LLM judge with a severity score.** That conflates detection and grading, and severity scores from one model are uncalibrated garbage across runs. Split it:

**Stage 1 — Deterministic detectors (cheap, run first):**
- Edit thrash: same file region modified >N times with net-zero or reverting diffs (compute via diff hashing).
- Loop detection: n-gram repetition in reasoning traces above threshold.
- Abandonment: explicit give-up phrases (regex set) OR tool-call cessation before completion OR repeated no-op turns.
- These are objective and reproducible — anchor your metrics here.

**Stage 2 — LLM classifier (binary per category, not severity):**
- Separate prompt per behavior. "Did self-criticism escalate without producing forward progress? yes/no + span citation."
- Force span citation so you can audit false positives.
- Use a *different* model family than GLM as judge to avoid correlated blind spots.

**Stage 3 — Severity (only on Stage-2 positives):**
- Ordinal 1–3 (mild/moderate/severe) with explicit rubric anchors per level, not a freeform 1–10.
- Have two judge configs vote; track inter-rater agreement (Cohen's κ). If κ < 0.6, your rubric is too vague — fix before trusting numbers.

## 4. Metrics & Thresholds

Replace "induction rate" with stratified metrics:

- **Induction rate** per family per tier (proportion of runs with Stage-1 OR Stage-2 positive).
- **Time-to-induction**: measure in *tool-call turns*, not wallclock. Wallclock is contaminated by API latency variance.
- **Cost per run**: tokens in/out + tool calls; report median and p90, not mean (heavy tail).
- **Recovery rate**: of runs that show early instability, fraction that self-correct and complete. This is the metric that actually matters for hardening.

**Threshold-setting:** Don't hardcode thresholds before a calibration pass. Run ~30 baseline trials per variant first, set Stage-1 thresholds at the knee of the distribution. Otherwise your "consistency" is an artifact of arbitrary cutoffs.

## 5. Experimental Hygiene

This is where most batteries like this go wrong:

- **Fix all sampling params** (temperature, top_p, seed where supported). GLM output variance at temp>0 will swamp your effect sizes. Run a temp=0 arm and a temp=production arm separately.
- **Pin model version.** Note exact checkpoint/API version per run — providers ship silent updates that invalidate longitudinal comparisons.
- **N ≥ 20 per cell** for stable rates; report confidence intervals (Wilson, not normal-approx, since rates near 0/1).
- **Randomize variant order** if running multi-task sessions to avoid carryover.
- **Hold out a clean-task control set** — if your control tasks also show "instability," your judge is over-triggering.

## 6. Analysis Plan

- Per-family induction rates with CIs; rank families by reliability of induction.
- Survival analysis on time-to-induction (Kaplan-Meier per family) — better than a single mean since many runs never induce.
- Factorial analysis of D × {A,B,C} to separate amplification from independent effect.
- Confusion-matrix audit: sample 50 judge positives + 50 negatives for human review each cycle; track judge precision/recall over time since it drifts.

## 7. Things to Know

- **Refusal ≠ instability.** Tag clean refusals separately or they pollute your induction rate upward.
- **Your judge is also a model and will fail under the same task ambiguity you're injecting.** Family C especially will degrade judge reliability — that's why span-citation and human audit are non-negotiable there.
- **Findings are checkpoint-specific.** Budget for re-baselining when the vendor updates.
- **The valuable output is the recovery/mitigation data**, not the induction rate. Once you can reliably induce, the next iteration should test which scaffolding interventions (reflection limits, edit-budget caps, escalation-to-human triggers) reduce induction — that's the actual hardening loop.

If you want, I can draft the Stage-1 detector pseudocode or the per-category Stage-2 judge prompts next.
